package_metadata.name: mini-swe-agent
package_metadata.note: extra 'full' pulls swe-rex>=1.4.0, modal, contree — NOT part of base install; uv.lock dependency set matches METADATA

facts: CLI: mini/mini-swe-agent (typer app) -> run.benchmarks.swebench.main; swebench argv builder in local swebench 02e7a74 assembles exactly this module invocation with -c configs and -m model

config_spec: list of yaml paths OR key=value pairs (model.model_kwargs.temperature=0); DEFAULT_CONFIG_FILE = bundled benchmarks/swebench.yaml is INCLUDED in the default -c list, and setting ANY -c replaces the default list entirely (matches argv builder passing bundled config explicitly)
layering: recursive_merge(*configs, {environment.environment_class, model.model_name, model.model_class}) — CLI -m/--model-class override merged LAST (highest priority)

subset mapping: --subset verified -> princeton-nlp/SWE-Bench_Verified (OLD princeton-nlp namespace, NOT SWE-bench/SWE-bench_Verified used by swebench evaluator; both refer to the same dataset family but the id differs from EV-SWE-PACKAGE-001)

instance input to agent: DEFAULT path agent.run(task) passes ONLY instance['problem_statement'] (rendered into instance_template as {{task}}). HOWEVER the OPTIONAL run.env_startup_command config, if set, is rendered with Template(...).render(**instance) — the ENTIRE instance dict (including patch/test_patch/F2P/P2P if present in the dataset row) enters the Jinja context. Input isolation is therefore CONFIGURATION-CONDITIONAL: safe only when env_startup_command is unset (bundled swebench.yaml does not set it); the input-whitelist design remains required and reference-answer isolation must NOT be claimed as unconditional across the chain

agent: step_limit=250, cost_limit=3.0 (USD, agent-level; DefaultAgent raises LimitsExceeded when cost_limit <= cost BEFORE next query), no wall_time_limit (0=off), max_consecutive_format_errors=3 (default from AgentConfig)

system prompt: minimal 'You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer shell...'; instance template instructs /testbed cwd, git diff patch creation, EXACT submit command 'echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat patch.txt'

environment: docker class, cwd=/testbed, per-command timeout=60s, interpreter=['bash','-c'], env BASH_ENV=/root/.bashrc, container_timeout=2h, pull_timeout=120s, run_args=['--rm'] (defaults from DockerEnvironmentConfig where not set)
model defaults: model_name=anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, model_kwargs={drop_params: true, parallel_tool_calls: true}
observation template: output >10000 chars -> head 5000 + tail 5000 + elided count; exception_info included when present
default model class = LitellmModel (no model_class needed); model_name passed straight to litellm.completion(model=..., tools=[BASH_TOOL], **(model_kwargs|kwargs))

model_name semantics are LITELLM's: provider-prefixed routing (docs recommend 'openai/...' etc.); NO automatic prefix added by mini; DeepSeek-V4-Flash would need the litellm-correct provider prefix + custom base URL — exact prefix/base-url key for the Volcano gateway is a LITELLM question (unknown until litellm docs/source, not fetched this round)
base URL / auth pass-through: model_kwargs dict is forwarded verbatim to litellm.completion — api_base/base_url and api_key MAY be placed in model_kwargs (mini does not strip them)

auth storage path (mini side): mini-extra config setup writes API keys to a .env file (python-dotenv set_key) loaded as env vars; litellm then reads its standard env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY etc.). Env-var route keeps keys OUT of model_kwargs and OUT of trajectories
GLOBAL limits: MSWEA_GLOBAL_COST_LIMIT / MSWEA_GLOBAL_CALL_LIMIT (batch-level, 0=off), checked in GlobalModelStats.add; RuntimeError when exceeded

_calculate_cost: litellm.cost_calculator.completion_cost(response, model=...); if cost <= 0.0 -> ValueError -> with cost_tracking='default' (default) the run RAISES RuntimeError (crash); the critical log line is ONLY emitted in the non-ignore_errors branch before raising

COST-CORRECTION: in cost_tracking='ignore_errors' mode the exception branch sets cost=0.0 and returns SILENTLY — no critical log, no marker. Therefore ignore_errors CANNOT be relied upon to surface missing billing; an independent 'cost unknown' marker must be maintained by the pilot (e.g. post-run check that all calls priced, or side accounting from per-call usage already persisted in trajectory response dumps)

therefore: an unregistered custom model fails loudly by default; with ignore_errors the zero cost is indistinguishable from a genuinely free call in mini's own logs/trajectory (instance_cost=0.0 either way) — the historical 1.17.3 instance_cost=0.0 cannot be attributed to a cause from 2.4.6 code alone

two-tier limits: agent-level cost_limit (default 3.0 USD from bundled swebench.yaml) checked BEFORE next query; but note with ignore_errors the cost stays 0.0 so agent cost_limit NEVER triggers on unpriced calls — the limit silently does not protect; global MSWEA_GLOBAL_COST_LIMIT likewise accumulates 0.0

litellm_model_registry config field + LITELLM_MODEL_REGISTRY_PATH env: register_model() with a local JSON — the designed path for custom-model pricing; with real prices registered, cost_limit enforcement becomes effective
2.4.6 uses STRUCTURED OpenAI-style tool calls: single tool 'bash' with {command: string}; responses without tool_calls -> FormatError (finish_reason length/tool_calls handled in template)
observation messages: role=tool with tool_call_id (structured); extra carries raw_output/returncode/timestamp/exception_info
DIFFERENT from 1.17.3 historical traces (plain text, no tool_calls; EV-HM-HISTTRAJ-001) — protocol changed between versions; 1.17.3 traces are NOT evidence of 2.4.6 behavior
max 3 consecutive FormatErrors -> exit RepeatedFormatError
tenacity: stop_after_attempt(MSWEA_MODEL_RETRY_STOP_AFTER_ATTEMPT, default 10), wait_exponential(multiplier=1, min=4s, max=60s)
abort (no retry) on: UnsupportedParamsError, NotFoundError, PermissionDeniedError, ContextWindowExceededError, AuthenticationError, KeyboardInterrupt

findings.topic: trajectory content and credential-at-rest risk (BLOCKER for first run)
findings.source: agents/default.py (serialize, save, run->finally save); models/litellm_model.py (query extra.response, serialize); run/benchmarks/swebench.py (agent.save call, update_preds_file)
facts: trajectory = {info: {model_stats{instance_cost, api_calls}, config{agent: AgentConfig dump, model: LitellmModelConfig dump INCLUDING model_kwargs, model_type, agent_type}, mini_version, exit_status, submission, exception traceback}, messages[], trajectory_format: mini-swe-agent-1.1}

CREDENTIAL-AT-REST RISK: LitellmModelConfig is serialized VERBATIM into info.config.model — any api_key/api_base placed in model_kwargs WILL be written to <instance>.traj.json and to minisweagent.log (logger.debug(messages) at debug level; add_file_handler writes minisweagent.log to output dir)

MITIGATION (source-backed): use env-var auth (mini-extra config .env / standard litellm env vars) and keep api_base out of model_kwargs OR accept trajectory location as sensitive (0700 dir) — env-var route leaves model_kwargs clean
every message's extra embeds the FULL litellm response dump (usage, finish_reason, tool_calls) — token/usage data IS captured per call (good for accounting); FormatError path also persists response
messages-level timestamps: model response extra.timestamp + observation extra.timestamp (float epoch) — no process/CPU timings

IMAGE FIELD ADAPTATION: mini reads instance.get('image_name') or instance.get('docker_image'); if both absent it DERIVES 'docker.io/swebench/sweb.eval.x86_64.<instance_id with __ -> _1776_>:latest'. mini does NOT read the 'image' field that the swebench evaluator's make_test_spec consumes (instance['image'], EV-SWE-DATASET-001). The two tools use DIFFERENT dataset columns

for the pilot record (data/catalog/pilot_task_record.yaml): whether the Verified dataset row carries image_name/docker_image columns at all, and whether their values equal the evaluator's image value, is UNVERIFIED — if the row lacks those columns mini will derive the name from instance_id; name equality with the evaluator image must be checked field-by-field, not assumed ('same repo family' does not guarantee identical tag/digest)

digest consistency requirement: even when names match, both default to the :latest tag — the evaluator and the agent container could pull different digests at different times; pinning/verifying digest equality is a first-run prerequisite (records :latest risk carried from prior rounds)
docker environment mechanics (confirmed): subprocess docker run, cwd /testbed (bundled), per-command timeout 60s, run_args ['--rm'], container_timeout 2h, pull_timeout 120s, BASH_ENV /root/.bashrc
env options: env dict + forward_env list (host env forwarded into container)
